title: FDA RSABE, fully replicate, CVwR 31%, ratio 0.90, n=36

oracle.arguments: power.RSABE(CV=0.31, theta0=0.90, n=36, design="2x2x4", regulator=reg_const("USER", r_const=log(1.25)/0.25, CVswitch=0, CVcap=Inf, pe_constr=TRUE), details=TRUE, nsims=1e5)
oracle.method_note: PowerTOST computes empirical power by simulating nsims studies from the distributional properties of the deciding statistics. be-stats analyses datasets, so the Python side simulates studies and applies the be-stats criterion to each. Two Monte Carlo estimates of one probability, compared at the only layer both expose.
oracle.regulatory_setting_note: r_const is FDA's log(1.25)/0.25 and the criterion is unchanged - SABE_test stays "fda", including its Em <- Em - SEs^2 bias correction. Only CVswitch is set to 0, which makes PowerTOST's p(BE-sABEc) the scaled criterion ALONE rather than the mixed decision. See VAL-FDA-HVD-001: comparing the mixed decision against the scaled criterion is what put this case 4.61 sigma out in PR #58, inside a tolerance that passed. CVcap=Inf reproduces FDA, which imposes no cap.

comparisons.tolerance_basis: DERIVED, and independent of the answer. Both sides estimate the same probability by simulation, so the difference between them has standard deviation sqrt(p(1-p)(1/n_python + 1/n_R)). Evaluated at the WORST CASE p = 0.5, which maximises p(1-p), and taken at four standard deviations: 4 * sqrt(0.25 * (1/20000 + 1/100000)) = 0.01549. Using worst-case p rather than the observed p means the tolerance was fixed before either side was run. UNCHANGED FROM PR #58: VAL-FDA-HVD-001 was a mismatch of quantities, not of tolerances, and retrofitting a tolerance to a resolved finding would leave the tolerance meaning nothing.

DERIVED, and independent of the answer. As for p_be_sabec: 4 * sqrt(0.25 * (1/20000 + 1/100000)) = 0.01549. PowerTOST's BEpe is evaluated over all simulations unconditionally, so this quantity was directly comparable under either regulator setting - which is why it agreed in PR #58 while p_be_sabec did not.

DERIVED, one-sided. The R side computes this in CLOSED FORM - sWR^2 * dfRR / sigma^2_wR is chi-square on dfRR = n - 2 = 34 degrees of freedom under the model both sides simulate, so P(sWR < 0.294) = pchisq(34 * 0.294^2 / log(1+0.31^2), 34) exactly. Only the Python side carries sampling error, so the tolerance is 4 * sqrt(0.25/20000) = 0.01414 at worst-case p = 0.5. Fixed before the run.

not_cross_checkable: The overall p(BE), and the mixed procedure generally. PowerTOST decides below the switch by a TOST on the same intra-subject contrast; FDA specifies Appendix C's mixed model, which be-stats records and refuses to approximate (see replicate_abe.py). Neither PowerTOST's convention nor be-stats' silence can validate the other.

The intermediate Howe quantities x, bound_x, y and bound_y. PowerTOST does not expose them for a dataset; it exposes only the probability that the criterion passed. They are checked instead against the FDA SAS in the tier-1A case FDA-HVD-RSABE-CRITERION-001.

sWR and the treatment contrast for any individual study. PowerTOST analyses no dataset, so there is nothing to compare them with. This is not a gap that can be closed by choosing different arguments: PowerTOST 1.5-7 exposes no dataset-level entry point for the FDA scaled procedures at all.
notes: Sits just above the 30 percent classification CV, so a substantial share of simulated studies land on either side of the sWR = 0.294 switch - about 43.5 percent, which p_below_switch now checks against the exact chi-square rather than leaving as a diagnostic. That share is precisely what made this case, and only this case, expose the quantity mismatch recorded as VAL-FDA-HVD-001: at CVwR 0.40 and 0.60 almost nothing falls below the switch, so the mixed decision and the scaled criterion coincide and the mismatch was invisible.
